newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kelon's 1996 net seen beating forecast.
newsitem.headline: Kelon's 1996 net seen beating forecast.

text.p: China's biggest refrigerator maker Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd is set to beat its own net profit forecast of 428 million yuan (HK$399 million) when it reports 1996 results on Friday, analysts said.

Estimates for the company, which listed in Hong Kong in July 1996, ranged from HK$400 million to HK$430 million, while the Estimate Directory put the consensus forecast at 428 million yuan, up 62 percent compared with 1995 net profit.
"Although the refrigerator industry (in China) is still hit by overcapacity, Kelon is an outperformer in the market," said Elka Ho, a China analyst at DBS Securities.

Kelon's profit margin rose by 0.5 of a percentage point in 1996 thanks to lower raw material and component costs, one analyst at a Japanese house said. The increased use of domestically produced compressors helped greatly in reducing costs, he added.
The amount of imported compressors used by the company fell to 55 percent for the first quarter of 1996 from 80.5 percent at the end of 1995, the company said in its listing prospectus.
Compressors accounted for about 28.8 percent of the company's total purchasing costs in calendar 1995.

Worries about competitive pressures hampered the company's stock market debut and its shares traded below the initial public offering price of HK$3.67 per share during the first four months of listing.
Concerns were shrugged off in December and the stock closed at HK$6.85 on Wednesday.
"Now people believe that the concern was overdone as people think its location would allow it to get good orders," said Ginny Chen, head of China research at Asia Equity.
Kelon is based in Shunde city at the Pearl River Delta in China's prosperous southern province of Guangdong.
The company's orders on hand total about 2.1 million units for 1997, more than its projected yearly production capacity of 1.8 million units.
Analysts said they expected 1996 orders to also have exceeded last year's annual capacity of 1.5 million units.
Kelon produced about 1.22 million refrigerators in 1995 and sold about 1.18 million. The sales accounted for about 13.4 percent of China's refrigerator market, Kelon's listing document showed.

Its Chengdu and Liaoning joint ventures, formed in late December and early 1997, would help Kelon meet the excess demand but it was unlikely to see a major increase in production until mid-1998, Chen said.
Analysts said they expected domestic and foreign competition to heat up over the next few years as production from Sino-foreign joint ventures came on stream starting in mid-1998.
But they said a good marketing network and a widely accepted brand name would put the company in a favourable position.
"It will take time for foreign joint ventures to develop a sales network and they are unlikely to overtake in the near term," DBS's Ho said.
"Kelon's product in terms of brand, prices and quality suit the Chinese market well, so we are not worried about competition at the moment," she added.
The analyst at the Japanese house also said Kelon used to sell its products to wholesalers and distributors but now was putting more emphasis on direct links with customers.
Kelon said last year it was setting up display centres in major retail outlets across China.
More than 95 percent of its sales were registered in China in 1995, the listing document said.
